source_value.trigger: The pointer travels from x137,y85 beside the Start date field to the caret of the 'All users' select at x338,y83 between 7.10s and 8.30s, then that select is activated: the dropdown panel is absent in frame 271 (9.000s) and fully drawn in frame 272 (9.033s).
source_value.start_state: 'History and notes' at 0.00s with Start date '1 May 2025', End date '31 Aug 2025', User 'All users', Type 'All types', 'Showing 100 of 346 results', and the first rows of the table (10 Sept 2025 08:19 / Jenny Simmons / Transaction - spend money / Edited); nothing on the page changes for the first 7.10s, where consecutive frames differ by at most 0.04/255 with no pixel differing by more than 25.
source_value.end_state: The same page at 14.967s with the User dropdown open over the table, showing 'Deselect all' and the ticked options 'Jenny Simmons' and 'System Generated'; the filter row, the 'Showing 100 of 346 results' count and every visible table row are unchanged behind the panel, and no filter has been applied.
source_value.continuity: Nothing outside the dropdown's own rectangle is repositioned or redrawn: the opening frame pair differs only inside x225-307, y94-154 (1121 pixels over 25/255, whole-frame mean 0.66/255), and from 9.400s to 14.333s 149 consecutive frames are byte-identical to media/state-3.png. The one whole-frame difference elsewhere, 0.88/255 at 8.333s with just 75 pixels over 25, is a codec keyframe refresh and moves nothing.
source_value.feedback: The dropdown panel itself is the only feedback, and it arrives already populated with both options ticked; no hover highlight, focus ring, spinner or busy indicator appears on the 'All users' control in any of the 449 frames, and because the 'Apply' button is never pressed the 'Showing 100 of 346 results' count never changes.
source_value.reduced_motion_equivalent: Not demonstrated: no motion-preference control appears in the excerpt, and the single transition it contains is a one-frame appearance with no animation for a reduced-motion mode to replace; the nonanimated equivalent retained here is the ordered three-frame set.
